facts.text: In United States construction, vehicles and mobile heavy equipment caused 7,681 deaths from 1992 to 2010, averaging about 404 deaths a year.
facts.quote: Vehicles and mobile heavy equipment caused 7,681 construction deaths from 1992 to 2010, about 404 a year.

facts.text: At United States road construction sites, most victims were workers on foot struck by vehicles or equipment.
facts.quote: At road construction sites most victims were workers on foot struck by vehicles or equipment

facts.text: At United States road construction sites, 131 deaths resulted from a vehicle or mobile equipment backing up.
facts.quote: 131 road-site deaths resulted from a vehicle or mobile equipment backing up [59].

facts.text: In United States construction in 2019, struck-by injuries caused 170 deaths, representing 15.4% of all construction deaths.
facts.quote: In 2019 struck-by injuries caused 170 construction deaths (15.4% of the total)

facts.text: In United States construction in 2019, nearly half (47.1%) of struck-by deaths involved transport vehicles.
facts.quote: In 2019 struck-by injuries caused 170 construction deaths (15.4% of the total) and nearly half (47.1%) involved transport vehicles [60, 61].

facts.text: In United States construction in 2020, struck-by incidents caused 150 deaths.
In United States construction in 2020, struck-by incidents caused 14,000 nonfatal injuries.
facts.quote: In 2020 struck-by incidents caused 150 deaths and 14,000 nonfatal injuries in construction

facts.text: Nonfatal claims from struck-by incidents in United States construction in 2020 incurred $1.4 billion in direct workers' compensation costs.
facts.quote: with $1.4 billion in direct workers' compensation costs for nonfatal claims [62].

facts.text: At United States road construction sites from 2005 to 2016, being struck by a vehicle or mobile equipment was the most common cause of death.
facts.quote: At road construction sites (2005 to 2016), being struck by a vehicle or mobile equipment was the most common cause of death

facts.text: Trucks were the top source of deaths at United States road construction sites from 2005 to 2016.
facts.quote: At road construction sites (2005 to 2016), being struck by a vehicle or mobile equipment was the most common cause of death, and trucks were the top source [63].
